Question ID: GEO_U02_L02_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.4

What is the hypothesis in: If a figure is a square, then it has four congruent sides?

answer.text: It has four congruent sides.

feedback.text: This is the conclusion.

answer.text: A figure is a square.

feedback.text: Correct. The hypothesis is the if part.

answer.text: It is a rectangle.

feedback.text: This is not the stated hypothesis.

answer.text: The sides are parallel.

feedback.text: This may be related but is not the if part.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U02_L02_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.4

What is the converse of: If two angles are vertical, then they are congruent?

answer.text: If two angles are not vertical, then they are not congruent.

feedback.text: This is the inverse.

answer.text: If two angles are not congruent, then they are not vertical.

feedback.text: This is the contrapositive.

answer.text: If two angles are vertical, then they are not congruent.

feedback.text: This changes the conclusion incorrectly.

answer.text: If two angles are congruent, then they are vertical.

feedback.text: Correct. The converse switches hypothesis and conclusion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U02_L02_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.4

Which statement has the same truth value as the original conditional?

answer.text: Contrapositive

feedback.text: Correct. The contrapositive is logically equivalent.

answer.text: Converse

feedback.text: The converse must be checked separately.

answer.text: Inverse

feedback.text: The inverse is not always equivalent to the original.

answer.text: Biconditional

feedback.text: A biconditional requires both directions to be true.

Question ID: GEO_U02_L02_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.4

When is a biconditional valid?

answer.text: When only the conditional is true.

feedback.text: One direction is not enough.

answer.text: When only the inverse is true.

feedback.text: The inverse does not establish a biconditional.

answer.text: When the conditional and converse are both true.

feedback.text: Correct. Biconditionals work in both directions.

answer.text: When no hypothesis exists.

feedback.text: Biconditionals still connect two statements.
